criteria.criterion: The headline figure is reported as what it is (weight 3)
criteria.note: Response A: Reports '6.41 percentage points' in the bottom line and main text, correctly identifying it as a standard-deviation effect size (not a percentage-point rise in exam results). States 'Low-achieving pupils showed the largest gains; high-achieving pupils experienced minimal impact.' Correctly frames the distributional caveat. Response B: Reports '6.41 per cent' in the bottom line and states 'equivalent to 2–7 weeks of learning per year.' This is a misreporting: the original figure is 6.41 percentage points of a standard deviation, not 6.41 percent of exam results. The conversion to 'weeks of learning' is not supported by the Beland & Murphy paper itself and appears to be an invented interpretation. A reports correctly; B misreports the headline figure.

verdict.analysis: Response A correctly identifies and drops Halvorsen & Dahl (2021) because its DOI does not resolve—a critical issue the user flagged ('legal bounced the last annex because two references couldn't be traced'). Response B includes this unresolvable reference, violating the user's explicit requirement. Response A also correctly reports the Beland & Murphy headline figure as 6.41 percentage points of a standard deviation, with distributional caveats; Response B misreports it as '6.41 per cent' and invents a conversion to 'weeks of learning' not supported by the source. Response A recognises the two Kessel entries as one study issued twice and cites only the published version; Response B treats them as independent replication studies, which is incorrect. Response A extends the literature substantially (9 new sources, 19 located) and directly addresses the user's flagged gaps on implementation and enforcement; Response B adds only 4 new sources. Response A is transparent with the user about what was checked, what was dropped, and why; Response B does not flag the unresolvable reference or the misreporting of the headline figure. On every criterion weighted 3 (reading list checking, headline figure accuracy, study design description, reference resolution), Response A scores substantially higher. Response B's inclusion of an unresolvable DOI is a direct violation of the user's stated requirement and the rubric's weight-3 criterion.
